input.text:
# The kafka-app's wiring: one dependency, Kafka, read through KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS, and what it
# is in each environment. The app never sees this file; it reads its setting as it always has.
version: 1
project: kafka-app

dependencies:
  kafka:
    description: The Kafka cluster the app talks to.
    settings:
      KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS: ${endpoint}

environments:
  # LawTwin's Kafka twin on this machine, its conformance level read from the report LawTwin
  # publishes for the release (level 3, answers), its seed fixed so a run replays byte for byte,
  # and its control plane published on 9644 for `ironframe twin kafka ...`. Build the image in the
  # lawtwin repository with `make image` until it is published.
  local:
    runtime: podman
    dependencies:
      kafka:
        twin:
          image: lawtwin/kafka
          version: 0.1.0
          conformance:
            level: answers
            report: conformance/lawtwin-kafka-0.1.0.json
          ports: [9092]
          seed: 42
          config:
            clock: frozen
          admin:
            port: 9644
    sync:
      - env_file:
          path: .env
    config_service:
      port: 8700

  # The real Kafka on this machine, run from Apache's image until the twin exists, with the
  # configuration service beside it on port 8700 (build its image with `make config-service-image`).
  local-broker:
    runtime: podman
    dependencies:
      kafka:
        real:
          endpoint: localhost:9092
          image: apache/kafka:4.1.0
          ports: [9092]
    sync:
      - env_file:
          path: .env
    config_service:
      port: 8700

  # The twin on AWS ECS Fargate, its endpoint read back from OpenTofu, and the settings synced to
  # AWS AppConfig for the app deployed beside it.
  staging:
    runtime: aws
    cloud:
      modules: ../../modules
      region: us-east-1
      vpc_id: vpc-0123456789abcdef0
      subnet_ids: [subnet-0123456789abcdef0, subnet-0fedcba9876543210]
    dependencies:
      kafka:
        twin:
          image: lawtwin/kafka
          version: 0.1.0
          conformance:
            report: conformance/lawtwin-kafka-0.1.0.json
          ports: [9092]
    sync:
      - aws_appconfig:
          region: us-east-1
          application: kafka-app
          profile: connections

  # The twin on GCP. Cloud Run serves only HTTP, so a Kafka twin, `protocol: tcp`, runs on a
  # Compute Engine instance with a reserved address it advertises to clients.
  staging-gcp:
    runtime: gcp
    cloud:
      modules: ../../modules
      project: kafka-app-staging
      region: europe-west1
      allowed_cidr_blocks: [10.0.0.0/8]
    dependencies:
      kafka:
        twin:
          image: lawtwin/kafka
          version: 0.1.0
          conformance:
            report: conformance/lawtwin-kafka-0.1.0.json
          ports: [9092]
          protocol: tcp
          seed: 42
          advertise_variable: LAWTWIN_ADVERTISE
    sync:
      - gcp_parameter_manager:
          project: kafka-app-staging
          parameter: kafka-app-connections

  # The real, hosted cluster: nothing is deployed, the settings point at it.
  production:
    runtime: aws
    cloud:
      region: us-east-1
      vpc_id: vpc-0123456789abcdef0
      subnet_ids: [subnet-0123456789abcdef0]
    dependencies:
      kafka:
        real:
          endpoint: b-1.kafka-app.example.internal:9092
          credentials: aws-secretsmanager:kafka-app/production/kafka
    sync:
      - aws_appconfig:
          region: us-east-1
          application: kafka-app
          profile: connections

files..env:
# Settings of environment local-broker of kafka-app, written by ironframe from the manifest or architecture.
# Edits are overwritten; change those instead.
KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS=localhost:9092
files..ironframe/local-broker/compose.yaml:
# Generated by ironframe from the manifest for environment local-broker of kafka-app; edits are overwritten by `ironframe up`.
name: ironframe-kafka-app-local-broker
services:
  ironframe-config-service:
    image: localhost/ironframe-config-service:0.1.0
    container_name: ironframe-kafka-app-local-broker-config-service
    ports:
    - 8700:8700
    environment:
      IRONFRAME_LISTEN: 0.0.0.0:8700
      IRONFRAME_SETTINGS: /etc/ironframe/settings.json
    volumes:
    - /work/.ironframe/local-broker/settings.json:/etc/ironframe/settings.json:ro,Z
    labels:
      io.ironframe.dependency: ironframe-config-service
      io.ironframe.environment: local-broker
      io.ironframe.kind: config-service
      io.ironframe.project: kafka-app
  kafka:
    image: docker.io/apache/kafka:4.1.0
    container_name: ironframe-kafka-app-local-broker-kafka
    ports:
    - 9092:9092
    labels:
      io.ironframe.dependency: kafka
      io.ironframe.environment: local-broker
      io.ironframe.kind: real
      io.ironframe.project: kafka-app

input.text:
# The kafka-app's wiring: one dependency, Kafka, read through KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS, and what it
# is in each environment. The app never sees this file; it reads its setting as it always has.
version: 1
project: kafka-app

dependencies:
  kafka:
    description: The Kafka cluster the app talks to.
    settings:
      KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS: ${endpoint}

environments:
  # LawTwin's Kafka twin on this machine, its conformance level read from the report LawTwin
  # publishes for the release (level 3, answers), its seed fixed so a run replays byte for byte,
  # and its control plane published on 9644 for `ironframe twin kafka ...`. Build the image in the
  # lawtwin repository with `make image` until it is published.
  local:
    runtime: podman
    dependencies:
      kafka:
        twin:
          image: lawtwin/kafka
          version: 0.1.0
          conformance:
            level: answers
            report: conformance/lawtwin-kafka-0.1.0.json
          ports: [9092]
          seed: 42
          config:
            clock: frozen
          admin:
            port: 9644
    sync:
      - env_file:
          path: .env
    config_service:
      port: 8700

  # The real Kafka on this machine, run from Apache's image until the twin exists, with the
  # configuration service beside it on port 8700 (build its image with `make config-service-image`).
  local-broker:
    runtime: podman
    dependencies:
      kafka:
        real:
          endpoint: localhost:9092
          image: apache/kafka:4.1.0
          ports: [9092]
    sync:
      - env_file:
          path: .env
    config_service:
      port: 8700

  # The twin on AWS ECS Fargate, its endpoint read back from OpenTofu, and the settings synced to
  # AWS AppConfig for the app deployed beside it.
  staging:
    runtime: aws
    cloud:
      modules: ../../modules
      region: us-east-1
      vpc_id: vpc-0123456789abcdef0
      subnet_ids: [subnet-0123456789abcdef0, subnet-0fedcba9876543210]
    dependencies:
      kafka:
        twin:
          image: lawtwin/kafka
          version: 0.1.0
          conformance:
            report: conformance/lawtwin-kafka-0.1.0.json
          ports: [9092]
    sync:
      - aws_appconfig:
          region: us-east-1
          application: kafka-app
          profile: connections

  # The twin on GCP. Cloud Run serves only HTTP, so a Kafka twin, `protocol: tcp`, runs on a
  # Compute Engine instance with a reserved address it advertises to clients.
  staging-gcp:
    runtime: gcp
    cloud:
      modules: ../../modules
      project: kafka-app-staging
      region: europe-west1
      allowed_cidr_blocks: [10.0.0.0/8]
    dependencies:
      kafka:
        twin:
          image: lawtwin/kafka
          version: 0.1.0
          conformance:
            report: conformance/lawtwin-kafka-0.1.0.json
          ports: [9092]
          protocol: tcp
          seed: 42
          advertise_variable: LAWTWIN_ADVERTISE
    sync:
      - gcp_parameter_manager:
          project: kafka-app-staging
          parameter: kafka-app-connections

  # The real, hosted cluster: nothing is deployed, the settings point at it.
  production:
    runtime: aws
    cloud:
      region: us-east-1
      vpc_id: vpc-0123456789abcdef0
      subnet_ids: [subnet-0123456789abcdef0]
    dependencies:
      kafka:
        real:
          endpoint: b-1.kafka-app.example.internal:9092
          credentials: aws-secretsmanager:kafka-app/production/kafka
    sync:
      - aws_appconfig:
          region: us-east-1
          application: kafka-app
          profile: connections
